title: 1993 AHSME Problem 27
statement: The sides of \(\triangle ABC\) have lengths \(6,\) \(8\) and \(10.\) A circle with center \(P\) and radius \(1\) rolls around the inside of \(\triangle ABC,\) always remaining tangent to at least one side of the triangle. When \(P\) first returns to its original position, through what distance has \(P\) traveled?

solutions.text: The center \(P\) remains one unit from the side it touches, so its path is the triangle formed by the three inward parallel lines at distance \(1.\) This triangle is similar to \(\triangle ABC.\) The original right triangle has area \(24\) and semiperimeter \(12,\) hence inradius \(\frac{24}{12}=2.\) The path triangle has inradius \(2-1=1,\) so its linear scale is \(\frac{1}{2}.\) Its perimeter, and therefore the distance traveled, is \[ \frac12(6+8+10)=12. \] Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: The center traces a smaller triangle whose sides are parallel to the original sides
The original \(6\)-\(8\)-\(10\) triangle has inradius \(2,\) while the center’s path has inradius \(1\)
